description.narrative: The objectives of the Project are to: (a) support the establishment of building blocks for the social safety net system; and (b) increase the access of poor and vulnerable households to targeted and adaptive cash transfers programs.

The objectives of the Social Safety Net Project for Senegal are to support the establishment of building blocks for the social safety net system and to provide targeted cash transfers to poor and vulnerable households. The project has two components. (1) Support to the development of the social safety net system component will support the government in the development of the social safety net system, as part of a national social protection framework. This component will support (i) the development of core instruments and procedures that will form the backbone of a social safety net system, and (ii) the strengthening of the institutional capacity of the Social Protection Delegation (DGPSN) and sectoral actors of the social safety net system. (2) Support to the national targeted cash transfer program for poor and vulnerable household?s component will support the expansion and strengthening of the National Cash Transfer Program (PNBSF). This component will finance: (i) monetary transfers to PNBSF beneficiary households; (ii) accompanying measures put in place by the DGPSN, sectoral actors and local institutions; and (iii) selected program management and evaluation costs.

title.narrative: Direct beneficiaries of climate-related emergency response

comment.narrative: This OI was included with AF3. This includes the response to floods, food insecurity, and fires. The target was overly exceeded, with 113,551 households benefitting from climate-related emergency response against a revised target of 85,000. This was due to the gradual piloting and scaling of three key programs and an enabling institutional framework.

title.narrative: Percentage of PNBSF beneficiary households who live below the poverty line

comment.narrative: The target was exceeded, with 93 percent of PNBSF beneficiary households living below the poverty line against a target of 80 percent.

The target was slightly exceeded, with 1,013,505 households registered in the RNU, surpassing the revised target of 1 million. All household identification data were collected before project closure and were utilized by the DGPSN for identification purposes in social safety net programs.

title.narrative: Share of PNBSF beneficiary households who attended the last four sensitization sessions

comment.narrative: The target was partially achieved, with 69 percent of PNBSF beneficiary households attending the last four sensitization sessions, falling short of the end target of 75 percent. In 2023 and 2024, with the funding of the PAFS and PAPSA, the DGPSN initiated the revision of the PNBSF's accompanying measures to broaden the number of topics covered during PNBSF awareness-raising sessions. The low number of themes may have led to a certain degree of beneficiary fatigue. The number of themes is being expanded and adapted to beneficiary needs, covering eight themes and 30 key practices on topics linked to human capital strengthening, economic inclusion, natural resource management, and resilience to climate shocks. The implementation of the revised set of accompanying measures will start in January 2025.

title.narrative: Percentage of complaints and grievances of the PNBSF registered in the MIS and resolved without delay

comment.narrative: This target was partially achieved. The MIS functionality "resolved without delay" became available in 2021. Since then, 100% of complaints (29,303) were resolved, 76 percent of which without delay, and 24 percent beyond 15 days after registration, as specified in the manual. The total number of complaints registered in the MIS since its deployment in 2018 amounts to 40,023, all of which were resolved.

actual.value: 76% of cases registered in the MIS resolved without delay

title.narrative: Number of PNBSF beneficiary households currently enrolled in the program

comment.narrative: The target was significantly surpassed, with a total of 355,000 households benefiting from the PNBSF, compared to a revised target of 300,000 households. In January 2023, the government opted to broaden the program's reach by including an additional 65,000 households with individuals who have disabilities who were already part of the CEC program. The original target of 300,000 households remained unchanged, as the project had recently undergone restructuring.

title.narrative: Share of local committees who understand the objectives of the RNU

comment.narrative: This indicator was designed to measure the community's level of understanding of the RNU. It was initially captured by an evaluation called Community Performance Scorecard (Carte Communautaire de Performance, CCP) conducted by a firm. The latest CCP was conducted in 2022, and a debriefing workshop was held in January 2023. As part of the extension of the RNU to 1 million households, all the local committees were updated on the RNU's objectives, as well as on the various stages of the extension process, which required a high level of involvement on their part as the community targeting process is one of the cornerstones of the extension process. Community targeting took place in the second half of 2023, and all communal committees received training on the extension process prior to deployment.

title.narrative: Number of households in the RNU benefitting from productive transfers

comment.narrative: This target was exceeded, with 59,766 households benefiting from the YKK program against a revised target of 50,000 households.

title.narrative: Households benefitting from temporary transfers in response to shocks

comment.narrative: A total of 598,261 households benefited from the assistance of shock response programs financed by the project, including 484,710 households benefitting from the exceptional cash transfer program in response to the impact of COVID-19 and inflation, which was the largest cash transfer operation ever being implemented in Senegal. The program was implemented before the second update of the RNU was completed, leading to some difficulties in reaching households whose RNU data were not up to date due to migration, change of phone numbers, change of household composition, etc. However, the exceptional cash transfer operation was able to reach 90 percent of its intended beneficiaries – accounting for 26 percent of the total population - in the 14 regions of the country with digital transfers.

title.narrative: Percentage of complaints and grievances of the RNU registered in the MIS and resolved as per the operations manual

comment.narrative: The target was exceeded, with 95 percent of complaints and grievances of the RNU registered in the MIS and resolved as per the operations manual against an end target of 80 percent.
The indicator measures the number of campaigns to update the RNU in its entirety and as per the manual of operations.

title.narrative: Impact of the PNBSF on women's decision making inside the household

comment.narrative: Women's decision-making is measured as the share of women who participate in household decisions concerning the following five aspects: education, health, nutrition, agriculture/livestock, and shock response. The impact evaluation of the PNBSF finds that 55 percent of the women are in charge of making the decisions within their household on these five aspects.

title.narrative: Number of regions visited every year for supervision mission by the PNBSF team of the sensitization sessions

comment.narrative: The target was fully achieved, with all of Senegal's 14 regions visited by supervision missions.

title.narrative: Number of households in the RNU benefitting from agricultural transfers

comment.narrative: The target was exceeded, with 28,957 households benefiting from the PRA against a target of 20,000 households.

title.narrative: Use of the Social Protection monitoring and evaluation platform

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the number of programs that used the RNU to identify and select program beneficiaries. While regular monitoring of this indicator was not conducted throughout the project, the actual target far exceeded the initial target of 17 programs, with 34 programs successfully using the RNU as a targeting tool. Some of these programs included the PNBSF, the agricultural resilience program, the Yokk Koom Koom program, nutrition programs, shock response programs and programs not implemented by the government but by partners such as UNICEF, GIZ or NGOs.

title.narrative: Quality of the management of the PNBSF

comment.narrative: This indicator measured the quality of the management of the PNBSF across six sub-indicators. Each indicator met was assigned one point. The points were not cumulative, with every point being calculated from zero every year. The sub-indicators included: (i) the MIS generates monitoring reports of the PNBSF with the monitoring indicators, (ii) the payment module in the PNBSF MIS automatically and electronically reconciles payment with the payment provider, (iii) on average, 80 percent of the sensitization sessions planned per year are implemented in the country, (iv) on average each regional coordinator has conducted at least 30 supervision missions over the year, (v) there was no delay in the payment of the cash transfer in any of the 4 trimesters in any department, and (iv) the satisfaction rate of the beneficiaries regarding the program is higher than 80 percent.

This indicator measures the general appreciation by the audit of the quality of the MIS based on two criteria: (i) the quality of the data (accuracy, completeness) and (ii) the use of each module by the users. The quality was measured on a scale from poor, to fair, average, satisfactory, and very satisfactory. The target was achieved since the RNU MIS contained data about a growing number of poor and vulnerable households throughout the entire country. These data were updated twice, and the various modules were used by a growing number of users over the course of the project. The value for this indicator was revised after the last ISR was published to reflect the completion of the community-based targeting process that allowed the RNU to include updated data about 1 million households.

title.narrative: Setting up the mechanism to respond to shocks

baseline.value: The pilot was carried out in 2017

target.value: The food security response program is implemented before the lean season starts

comment.narrative: As shown by the implementation of the exceptional cash transfer program in response to the impact of Covid-19 and inflation, the GoS successfully set up mechanisms to respond to shocks. Although the initial focus was on responding to food insecurity, the project quickly surpassed this objective by demonstrating the ability of the social protection system to respond to a wide range of shocks (climatic or economic). Not only did the project support the establishment of the tools for a rapid and effective response, but it also contributed to the institutionalization of adaptive social protection and the clarification of mandates between the various social protection agencies. Finally, it supported the establishment of an early shock response mechanism relying on objective data to mitigate the risk of a food insecurity crisis should severe drought conditions arise.

actual.value: The government created the FSN with a clear mandate to respond to shocks using RNU-based targeting, digital cash transfers and a trigger-based mechanism for early implementation.
